blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Slicing the Pizza
blocks.content: A fraction represents a **part of a whole**. When you cut a pizza into 8 equal slices and eat 3, you've eaten 3/8 of the pizza. The top number (numerator) counts how many pieces you have. The bottom number (denominator) tells you how many equal pieces the whole was cut into. Fractions are everywhere: time (quarter past), money (half price), and cooking (3/4 cup).

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: Adding and Subtracting
blocks.content:
The golden rule: you can ONLY add fractions when the denominators are the same!

• **Same denominator:** Just add/subtract the tops. 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8.
• **Different denominators:** Find the LCM, convert both fractions, then add.
• **Mixed numbers:** Convert to improper fractions first (e.g., 2 1/3 = 7/3), then add.
• Always simplify your final answer!

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Multiplying and Dividing
blocks.content:
Multiplication is actually easier than addition!

1. **To multiply:** Multiply the tops together, multiply the bottoms together. (2/3) * (4/5) = 8/15.
2. **To divide:** FLIP the second fraction and multiply! (2/3) / (4/5) = (2/3) * (5/4) = 10/12 = 5/6.
3. Always simplify by dividing top and bottom by their GCD.

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Mixed Number Subtraction
blocks.content:
Calculate 3 1/4 - 1 2/3.

**Step 1:** Convert to improper: 13/4 - 5/3.
**Step 2:** Find LCM of 4 and 3 = 12.
**Step 3:** Convert: 39/12 - 20/12.
**Step 4:** Subtract numerators: 19/12.
**Step 5:** Convert back: 1 7/12.

**Final Answer: 1 7/12.**

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The most devastating fraction mistake: adding the denominators! When students see 1/3 + 1/4, they write 2/7. **COMPLETELY WRONG!** The denominators must be made the same (LCM = 12), giving 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12. Also, when dividing fractions, students forget to flip the SECOND fraction. You flip the one you're dividing BY, not the first one!
